fatal_errors: No supporting prior evidence is cited despite the explicit requirement.
The experiment does not specify lower Pt loading for the ALD catalyst, so it cannot test the claimed reduction in PGM consumption.
The proposed intervention does not reconstruct the target's closed-loop high-throughput discovery of aged multielement alloy catalysts.
Testing conditions and species-resolved performance criteria are too vague to establish automotive-exhaust activity under a defined feed.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective and proposes a reasonable comparison against an impregnated Pt catalyst, but it is scientifically and evidentially underdeveloped. It replaces the target intervention—machine-learning-guided discovery and process optimization of multielement alloys on La-doped alumina—with ALD-derived Pt single atoms on ceria-zirconia. Its generic dispersion and sintering mechanism does not match the target's ageing-induced Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction, hydrocarbon-assisted NO reduction, or alkalinity- and temperature-dependent multimetal formation. The experiment could compare activity and ageing stability, but without defined exhaust composition, ageing protocol, conversion metrics, matched versus reduced Pt loadings, or quantitative thresholds, it cannot decisively test the full activity–durability–PGM-consumption claim. The complete absence of cited evidence makes the alternative unsupported rather than a well-supported plausible alternative.
